top_choice_rationale: P001 rewards a distinct, independently reproduced measurement advance: magic-wavelength lattice trapping removed Doppler, recoil and Stark shifts together and took neutral-atom clocks to about 1e-18, confirmed in several laboratories with well-understood systematics. Credit to Katori (proposal and first demonstrations) and Ye (performance frontier) is the cleanest on the table, provided the citation stays on the lattice clock and its uncertainty and not on the frequency comb or optical clocks generally. P002 is sound physics with a restricted citation but has overlap with the 2016 prize and an arguable credit boundary around Hasan and Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang; I still prefer it to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; I work in astroparticle physics at KTH with no known tie to Katori, Ye, Kane, Mele or Molenkamp, and the atomic and condensed-matter judgements rely on colleagues.
